Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) transfer learning and cross-domain adaptation


Overview of Cross-Domain Adaptation in NILM
- Definition : Cross-domain adaptation solves the performance drop that occurs when a NILM model trained in one location (source domain) is applied to a new environment (target domain) with different user habits, appliance models, or backgrou
[DTU Research Database]
: Cross-domain adaptation solves the performance drop that occurs when a NILM model trained in one location (source domain) is applied to a new environment (target domain) with different user habits, appliance models, or background loads.
- Core Problem : Domain shift arises from variations in sampling rates, electrical noise, and appliance signatures across different households or commercial floors.


Key Methodological Approaches
- Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) : Utilizes adversarial networks and maximum mean discrepancy to align feature distributions between a labeled source domain and an unlabeled target domain.
